findings: The gap is a cliff at >= 40 connections / >= 100 crossings; at 10M work the strict first pass plus reachability floods use the whole budget and negotiation never starts.
At 200M work (single variant) the 24 srj19 gap boards reach 95.7 % of connections and 6 are clean; most failures then are 'ripped up and not routed again' and rip-cap rejections.
Fast bends (approximate bend costs) give +4 pts routed and 0 -> 12 % clean at equal wall time; rip limit 40 + 40 passes: 33 % -> 54 % clean at 50M on the gap boards.
tscircuit's solutions used as hard/soft guides did not help: topology alone is not the missing piece; the lattice cannot reproduce its off-grid geometry.
Deep-ring-first and longest-first orders, global router corridors, a coarser/finer lattice and negotiating from the first pass all lose at equal work.
GPU fields give the identical result 1.7x faster on one board, but slower with 12 boards in parallel (contention).
Portfolio of 8 variants (50M each, 8 threads, median 135 s wall) closes 10 of the 24 srj19 boards that one variant misses: about 186/200 = 93 % against tscircuit's 92 %.
Layer assignment from crossing chords (396 crossings -> 128 on one layer) does not help srj20 (18 % -> 14 % clean on gap boards).

fanout31 needed importer modelling, not routing changes: planes as zones, per-connection exit layers, far-component pads as keep-outs, closed layers as rule areas, outline margin. Three trial cases then route completely.
srj20 failures are dominated by negotiation churn ('ripped up by X and not routed again', 585 of ~1,170 failures); 24 seeded variants on one hard board all stop at 33-40 of 52.

The K230 'dead terminals' were a modelling bug: several buses' breakout points share coordinates and differ only by layer, so overriding their layer from connectionExitTargets stacked terminals on one layer. Without the override all 65 terminals escape and K230 goes 0/12 -> 12/12 with the portfolio.

Preferred layer directions (even layers horizontal, odd vertical; --layer-dir-pen 0.3) are the first structural gain on srj20: gap boards 28 -> 40 % clean, 87.7 -> 89.8 % routed; swapping the directions is neutral. Applied automatically only to breakout boards (>= 70 % of connections touch a ball-grid package, two layers): on ordinary boards it cost 2.4 points of completion.
Final: ctest 254/254, quick/mid byte-identical. srj19 188/200 (94.0 %) beats tscircuit 92.0 %; fanout31 60/72 beats 48/72; srj20 133/200 (66.5 %) is 24 boards short of 157.
M15: plain negotiation thrashes (sample069 30 M: routed count wobbles 30-41 for 40 s); as transactions (rip only if the victims re-route) it climbs: 41 -> 50 of 53.
M15: the work budget counts a reachability-flood cell like an A* expansion, but a flood cell costs far less time: txn + reach-check 2 gets 52.6 % clean in 137 s/board against 40 % in 71 s for plain.
M15: on the 76 boards P2 leaves open, 100 M work one variant: plain 5 clean, txn 9; boards of 70+ connections stay 10-30 connections short.
